source: library-report:SLEEP DEPRIVATION.md submarket C (followup.md run) + prompt.md stages 1-6
submarket: C. Parents' sleep - how exhausted parents divide the night

finding.headline: How exhausted parents divide the night is a parent operating-system problem, not a baby-sleep problem
finding.problem: A newborn wakes every night, but nobody has agreed in advance whose turn it is - so every single night is renegotiated by exhaustion between two adults running on no sleep.
finding.recurring_situation: Baby wakes at 2am. Mother is already awake feeding anyway; partner sleeps through. Nobody 'owns' the night, so the default becomes she owns all of it.
finding.person: [HYPOTHESIS] First-time mother 0-12 weeks postpartum, breastfeeding or mixed-feeding, partner works weekdays and sleeps through the night; no overnight family help in the house.
finding.trigger: Return of partner to work after leave - nights silently become 100% hers without a conversation.
finding.failed_attempt: 'Asking for help' - produced one-off gestures (he took the baby one Saturday morning) instead of a system; resentment now builds in silence because re-raising it feels like complaining.
finding.emotional_stake: She is not just tired - she keeps score alone. Every uninterrupted hour he gets feels like proof her exhaustion is invisible, and saying so makes her the difficult one.
finding.desired_outcome: A written, pre-agreed night roster both adults follow without renegotiation - she gets a protected block of real sleep and does not have to ask tonight, or any night.
evidence_quotes: [MODEL INFERENCE] composite of recurring community voices: 'I asked for help once and he watched the baby while I did everything else.'
[MODEL INFERENCE] composite: 'We are roommates who pass a baby back and forth at 3am.'
mechanism_hypotheses: A written roster removes the emotional labour of asking (negotiation becomes pre-agreed default)
Reframing partner from helper to co-manager upgrades his status instead of requesting charity
Milk hand-off scheduling makes the mother's protected block physically real
A sleep banker makes invisible exhaustion visible and tradeable
finding.competition_notes: Existing competitors sell baby-sleep training; none own the parents' night-division OS angle. Differentiation = mechanism + cultural coding + safety rigor, not market emptiness.

signals_observed: URGENCY: the problem repeats every single night; sleep debt compounds within days [MODEL INFERENCE]
FAILED_ATTEMPTS: 'asking for help' pattern documented repeatedly across submarket C research
IDENTITY_THREAT: being the default parent around the clock threatens her sense of self and partnership equality
IMMEDIATE_SPEND: entry-price impulse purchase plausible for a system promising tonight's relief

disposition.rationale: Distinct situation (night division between adults) + distinct meaningful transformation (protected sleep via written roster). Validated and scored 88/100 in the postpartum naming audit; built as V06 'Every Night, Just Me' - live on platform as transformation #84 / system #85 / product #86.
